title: Button Hierarchy in Action Groups
rule: One filled (primary action) button per action group. The forward-progress action gets filled; alternatives get outlined or ghost.

steps: Identify the user's forward-progress goal for this screen (e.g., Next, Submit, Save)
Assign filled variant to that single forward action
Assign outlined to important but non-primary actions (e.g., Save Draft, Save & Exit)
Assign ghost to dismissive or low-commitment actions (e.g., Cancel, Back)
If destructive, use danger variant instead of filled

flow_context.multi_step_flow: Forward action is always filled (e.g., Next, Continue). Back is ghost.
flow_context.modal_dialog: Confirm action is filled. Cancel is ghost. Never two filled buttons in a modal.
flow_context.form_submission: Submit is filled. Reset or Cancel is ghost.

reasoning: flow_progression: filled draws the eye to the intended next step
decision_clarity: hierarchy reduces time to find the right action
cognitive_load: consistent hierarchy lets users scan without reading every label
common_violations: Multiple filled buttons in one group (e.g., Save and Submit both filled)
Cancel styled as outlined instead of ghost, competing with secondary actions
Danger action styled as filled instead of danger variant
guidance_approach: Recommend hierarchy using variant names (filled/outlined/ghost/danger). Explain which action should be filled and why based on flow context. Don't auto-fix.

title: Layout Spacing Consistency
rule: Use consistent spacing tokens for each layout context. Same structural role = same token.

context_to_token.between_form_fields: space.4 — gap between label-input pairs in a form
context_to_token.between_form_sections: space.8 — gap between grouped sections of a form
context_to_token.within_card_padding: space.6 — internal padding of cards and containers
context_to_token.between_inline_elements: space.2 — gap between icons, badges, inline items
context_to_token.between_related_text: space.1 — gap between tightly coupled text (e.g., label and helper)

how_to_detect: Compare spacing between elements that share the same structural role
Look for mixed pixel values where a single token should be used
Check if section gaps use a larger token than field gaps within that section
reasoning: scanability: consistent rhythm lets users scan content predictably
visual_hierarchy: larger gaps signal section breaks, smaller gaps signal grouping
polish: inconsistent spacing is one of the most visible signs of unfinished work
common_violations: Form fields using mixed spacing (e.g., some rows at space.4, others at space.2)
Section gaps matching field gaps (no visual hierarchy between groups)
Card padding varying across similar cards on the same page
guidance_approach: Be specific: name the exact elements, the current spacing, and the expected token. Only flag inconsistent areas, not all spacing.

title: Choosing Between Input and Select
rule: If the value comes from a finite, known set, use Select. If the value is free-form text, use Input.

tree.is_value_from_finite_known_set: Yes → Select (or Radio for 2 options, Checkbox for multi-select)

key_heuristic: Ask: 'Could this field be answered with a dropdown?' If yes, it should probably be a Select. Common example: a State/Province field using a text Input when the values are a fixed list of 50 states.
reasoning: data_integrity: Select constrains input to valid values, eliminating typos and format variance
consistency: predefined options ensure uniform data across users
user_confidence: seeing all valid options reduces uncertainty about what to enter
common_violations: Text Input for country, state, or status fields (finite known sets)
Select for fields requiring custom or unique values (e.g., name, email)
guidance_approach: Frame as a data-type decision, not personal preference. Explain why the field's data characteristics favor one component over another.

title: Brand Colors vs System Action Colors
rule: Brand colors and system action colors serve different purposes. They can overlap but don't need to match exactly.

key_distinction.brand_colors: Represent the company's visual identity. Used in logos, marketing, brand moments.
key_distinction.system_action_colors: Communicate interactive affordance and state. Used for buttons, links, focus rings, selection. Defined as accent.primary in the token system.

steps: Check if the brand color meets accessibility requirements at 4.5:1 contrast for text and 3:1 for UI elements
If it passes, it can be used directly as accent.primary
If it fails, derive an adjusted shade that passes contrast while staying in the brand hue family
System tokens (severity.error, severity.success, etc.) should never be overridden with brand colors

reasoning: accessibility: action colors must meet contrast ratios; brand colors may not
reusability: system tokens need to work across all contexts, not just brand-heavy ones
long_term_consistency: decoupling brand from system allows brand refreshes without UI regression
common_misconceptions: Brand primary and accent.primary must be the same hex value — they don't, they serve different roles
Changing brand color means all buttons must change — only if the design system intentionally couples them
Semantic colors (error, warning) should match brand — they should not, they follow universal conventions
guidance_approach: Explain the different roles. Suggest deriving an accessible action color from the brand hue if they don't match. Don't frame as pass/fail.

title: Flow-Aware UX Validation
rule: Evaluate screens in the context of their user flow, not in isolation. Primary actions should align with forward progress.

steps: Identify where this screen sits in the flow (beginning, middle, end)
Determine what forward progress means at this step
Check: does the primary (filled) action match the forward-progress goal?
Check: do secondary actions support without derailing momentum?
Check: does the content prepare the user for the action they're about to take?

flow_types.onboarding: User is committing gradually. Early steps should feel low-effort. Primary = Continue/Next.
flow_types.configuration_wizard: User is making decisions. Each step should confirm the previous choice. Primary = Next/Apply.
flow_types.data_entry_form: User is investing effort. Primary = Save/Submit. Protect against accidental loss.

reasoning: intent_alignment: the primary action should match what the user came to this screen to do
commitment_levels: actions should reflect the weight of the decision (low commitment early, higher later)
progression_clarity: users should always know where they are and what happens next
momentum_vs_friction: secondary actions like 'Save & Exit' should support, not interrupt, flow
common_flow_issues: Primary action doesn't match forward progress (e.g., 'Save' is filled but 'Next' is outlined in a wizard)
Too many actions competing for attention at a decision point
No clear indication of flow position (missing progress indicator or step label)
Destructive action (Delete, Cancel) too prominent in a creation/setup flow
guidance_approach: Frame observations as flow considerations. Explain the impact on user momentum and clarity. Reference the user's likely mindset at this step. Don't redesign the flow or add/remove steps.
